title: Use case diagram
explanation: Shows developer actions and the boundaries of the AI provider and isolated runner.

title: Class diagram
explanation: Core persisted entities and service responsibilities. The complete column dictionary is in the database schema.

title: Object diagram
explanation: Illustrative snapshot of a workflow paused for architecture review; identifiers here are explanatory examples.

title: Component diagram
explanation: One modular application, one relational database and one separate trusted runner. Agent modules are Python functions.

title: Composite structure diagram
explanation: Internal collaboration of the orchestrator component; ports are logical interfaces rather than separate network services.

title: Deployment diagram
explanation: Local execution has a VM boundary for generated code. A free temporary tunnel exposes only the authenticated application.

title: Package diagram
explanation: Source dependencies follow the modular monolith layout. The API never imports the sandbox executor.

title: Profile diagram
explanation: Design vocabulary used in this project. Stereotypes describe responsibilities; enforcement is implemented in validation, transactions and runner constraints.

title: Activity diagram
explanation: Full workflow includes explicit human gates and a conditional repair loop. Review-only workflows omit generation stages.

title: State machine diagram
explanation: Persisted workflow status transitions, including a lease-expiry recovery path and cancellation.

title: Sequence diagram
explanation: Optimistic approval binds both artifact content and project revision, preventing a stale browser action from committing different work.

title: Communication diagram
explanation: Numbered messages express collaboration around an approved test run. This uses object notation for UML communication links.

title: Interaction overview diagram
explanation: High-level references to detailed interactions. Decisions route complete generation, review-only or repair without running every agent.

title: Timing diagram
explanation: Illustrative ordering only; the horizontal units are logical ticks, not measured latency or a performance benchmark.

title: Database ER diagram
explanation: All thirteen PostgreSQL tables are included. Project ownership is resolved through users and projects for every API operation.
